newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Act NZ urges National not to give away tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Act NZ urges National not to give away tax cuts.

text.p: Rodney Hide, finance spokesman for the free-market Act New Zealand Party, urged the caretaker National Party government on Wednesday not to trade away planned tax cuts in coalition negotiations with nationalist New Zealand First.

"The tax cuts and spending programme laid out in the Pre-Election Economic and Fiscal Update (in September) should be National's bottom line," Hide said in a letter to caretaker Finance Minister Bill Birch, a copy of which was made public.
Backing down on the second round of tax cuts, due to take effect on July 1, 1997, would betray National's voters and "bring the political process into further disrepute", he said.
Staying with the spending programme outlined before the election would bring lower interest rates, a lower New Zealand dollar and relief to farmers, businesspeople and householders, Hide said.
"The market expectation fuelled by your comments is that spending is to increase. Interest rates and the dollar have stayed high as a result. A strong announcement now would bring immediate relief."
Media reports on Wednesday said National was poised to defer the tax cuts as the price of a deal with NZ First, freeing up a further NZ$1.1 billion for social spending.
Hide urged Birch to present to New Zealand First leader Winston Peters a "bottom line" set of policies with a deadline for deciding between Labour and National.
Peters, who holds the balance of power with 17 MPs, has been negotiating with both parties since an inconclusive general election on October 12.
Act, with eight MPs, has indicated it will support National, which has 44 seats in the 120-member parliament.
